target.role: fresh whole-journey contender discovery through current September 2026 releases, an emerging hand-played electro-percussion field and overlooked rhythm-reconfiguration catalogues
target.purpose: Test whether live-drum acceleration, hand-played groove switching, methodical accumulation, delayed beat arrival, skeletal syncopation or deliberate near-stasis gives the following formation new work rather than merely adding another internal turn.
target.position: Whole 32-track journey; preserve Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer. Treat placements as candidate-specific hypotheses and do not reopen untriggered PARKED identities.

explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 53 named tracks, releases and review entries across September 2026 current-release coverage, the emerging Gloorp hand-played electro-percussion field, Beatrice M.'s Sinking, Marina Herlop's Dja Dja preview, Kali Malone's Burning Song preview, Livity Sound, Rival Consoles' Persona, Björk's Homogenic and adjacent catalogue branches; attributed criticism and release metadata only; no audio audition.
sourceWindows: CURRENT: The Guardian's September 4, 2026 electronic survey supplied Silvan Strauss — That's Who?!? (Fast Barista) and Kali Malone — Heavy With Fruit; Pitchfork's September 8 Selects and July 1 Marina Herlop announcement supplied current-release windows. https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/sep/04/add-to-playlist-the-churning-darkness-of-barcelona-producer-nueen-and-the-weeks-best-new-tracks https://pitchfork.com/story/fine-djrum-miimii-kds-and-more-this-weeks-pitchfork-selects-playlist https://pitchfork.com/news/marina-herlop-readies-new-album-dja-dja

ADJACENT / EMERGING: Pitchfork's Gloorp 'Em Up review supplied exact hand-played footwork, bongo and delayed-beat candidates; Beatrice M.'s Sinking was inspected but prior local inspiration state already retained its strongest exact tracks, so it was not recycled. https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/gloorp-gloorp-em-up https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/beatrice-m-sinking

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE: Pitchfork reviews of Rival Consoles — Unfolding, Livity Sound and Björk's Homogenic supplied methodical polyrhythmic accumulation, skeletal syncopation and destructive four-on-the-floor rupture routes. https://pitchfork.com/reviews/tracks/rival-consoles-unfolding https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/18622-livity-sound-livity-sound https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/bjork-homogenic
FRESHNESS CHECK: exact repository search found no durable state for the nine requested identities. Runs 124–128 selected ecosystems and untriggered PARKED entries were excluded.
exclusions: Canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects, untriggered PARKED revisits, existing utility discoveries and unresolved prior leads without materially new identity evidence were excluded.

Runs 124–128 selected ecosystems were not retried: Azu Tiwaline, Pugilist, Black Bananas, Djrum, Rrose, Ripatti, Nondi_, Beatrice Dillon, Lechuga Zafiro, Skee Mask, Verraco, Jump Source, Rian Treanor/Ocen James and DJ Cinéma Quartier Latin.

Fine — Everything in the Shade was screened but did not clear the lead floor because the exact source described harmonic and vocal slipperiness without a credible rhythmic/structural route into this volume. Ambient, jazz and rock entries without a concrete volume-belonging hypothesis were excluded.
No Spotify connector, raw audio, audio-feature inference or invented identity was used.
